title: Rollback Signal Harmonizer for Multi‑SLO Canary & A/B Rollouts
creator: Aisha Campbell
description: Objective: Build a robust, tunable subsystem (the 'Rollback Signal Harmonizer') that ingests multiple SLO signals (latency p50/p95/p99, request error rate, token cost delta, throughput) across canary, A/B, and shadow traffic and emits a single rollback recommendation with explainability for Console and automated actuators. The harmonizer must support per-model policy, per-customer sensitivity, and context-aware threshold gating to avoid noisy rollbacks during transient noise or traffic spikes.
background: Current canary rollout tooling uses independent threshold checks per metric and per-cohort which has produced both false positives (rollbacks triggered by transient p99 spikes) and false negatives (combined small regressions across latency and token cost that individually were below thresholds but caused unacceptable unit-economics regressions). We need a combined signal approach that normalizes metrics, accounts for baseline variance, and produces a confidence score plus human-readable rationale.
proposal: 1) Compute z-score style normalized deltas for each SLO relative to rolling baseline windows (configurable: 1h/6h/24h). 2) Weight SLOs with tunable importance (customer or project default weights: latency 0.4, error_rate 0.35, token_cost 0.15, throughput 0.1). 3) Aggregate into a single rollback_score between 0-100. 4) Apply hysteresis windows and minimum observation counts to prevent acting on single-point spikes. 5) Support policy types: conservative (high hysteresis, higher thresholds), balanced, aggressive. 6) Emit structured explanation string and top contributing signals for the Console and incident timelines. 7) Allow offline tuning via historical replay and backtests and an online A/B to evaluate precision/recall of rollback decisions.
acceptance_criteria: Rollback subsystem computes rollback_score and exposes it via /v1/rollout/signals for canaries
Default policy reduces false-positive rollback rate by >=50% on historical 2024-12 regression dataset compared to independent-threshold baseline
Rollback recommendations include top-3 contributing metrics and normalized delta in the UI
Automated actuator honors minimum observation count and hysteresis; no rollbacks triggered by single-sample p99 spikes in 95% of tested scenarios
Backtest harness available in repo with ability to replay traffic, tune weights, and produce precision/recall and cost impact reports
experiment_plan: Phase A (offline): implement scorer and run batch replay on 6 months of anonymized canary data to sweep weights and hysteresis settings. Phase B (shadow): run scorer in parallel to production decision path for 2 weeks and collect signals. Phase C (live A/B): enable automated rollback actuator for a small percentage (5%) of canaries with conservative policy. Evaluate precision/recall and RPO impact before expanding to balanced/aggressive policies.
rollout_plan: 1) Launch scorer API (read-only) and Console visualization behind feature flag. 2) Run shadow for 2 weeks and collect feedback. 3) Enable actuator for 5% canaries with conservative policy + human approval workflow. 4) Increase to 20% and enable auto-rollback for low-risk workloads. 5) Add customer-level sensitivity and opt-out controls in Console.
monitoring_and_alerting: Create traceable events for score changes, and new high-priority alert when rollback_score > 80 for > 10 minutes on any canary with potential customer impact. Add dashboard panels: rollback_score heatmap, contributing metric breakdown, false-positive timeline. Wire alerts to on-call and to Console rollout page. Add audit log entry for any automated actuator decisions.
data_requirements: Baseline windows require per-route time-series for latency histograms, error counts, token counts, and throughput at 1m resolution. Backtest harness needs access to 6 months of anonymized canary traces and billing token cost estimates per model variant.
api_contracts: New endpoint: GET /v1/rollout/signals?canary_id={id}&window=1h returns: rollback_score (float), contributing_signals (list of strings), baseline_windows, computed_zscores. For this ticket we expose the endpoint as read-only; actuator integration is a follow-up task. All responses are logged to rollout audit topic.
risks_and_mitigation: Risk: Overfitting weights to historical regressions leading to missed real regressions. Mitigation: keep holdout dataset and require recall >=85% on holdout; require manual approval for critical customers. Risk: noisy metrics from upstream aggregation gaps. Mitigation: minimum observation counts and fallback to per-route thresholds.
security_and_compliance_notes: No customer PII required for score computation; only aggregates used. Backtest harness will use anonymized IDs. If a customer requests their model-level sensitivity, we will require appropriate access controls (RBAC) and audit logging.

next_steps: 1) Merge scorer API to integration branch. 2) Provision backtest dataset access for the team. 3) Schedule shadow run and add dashboard panels. 4) Draft Console copy for explanation strings and opt controls.
notes_for_reviewers: Focus review on z-score window sizing and default weights. Consider whether token_cost should be normalized by recent throughput to avoid skew when throughput rapidly changes.
implementation_notes: Keep scoring logic isolated in rollout-scorer service; expose lib for on-prem Private deployments. Use streaming aggregator to compute rolling baselines to minimize storage. Implement unit tests for z-score edge cases and end-to-end backtest notebooks.
estimated_impact: Expected to reduce unnecessary rollbacks by >=50% and reduce unit-token cost regressions not caught by single-metric thresholds. Should improve confidence for broader automated rollout adoption.
blocking_issues: Need anonymized canary traces access and a Console visualization slot. Ops to confirm retention policy for 1m-resolution timeseries.
